articles.title: How to spot a psychopath: ‘It’s like the difference between a domestic cat and a wild cat’
articles.summary: People with persistent predatory personalities cause an inordinate amount of pain. Recently, our shared understanding of them has grown – and it could help protect us.
body: The classic checklist for psychopathy was developed in 1980 by Prof Robert Hare, who is still the recognised giant of the territory. The 20 traits, which ranged from pathological lying to a lack of empathy, were based entirely on prison populations. This worked because not only did Hare have the benefit of a large sample, with pronounced psychopathic behaviours, but he was able to compare interviews and self-reporting with data collected about the individuals – so inconsistencies could be identified.
points: People with persistent predatory personalities cause an inordinate amount of pain.
Recently, our shared understanding of them has grown – and it could help protect us.

articles.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for saffron and tomato rice | A kitchen in Rome
articles.summary: Laborious to harvest and extortionately priced, the sunset-coloured stigmas of the saffron crocus have an extraordinarily warm, pungent taste. Fortunately, however, a little goes a very long way … The saffron crocus has six lilac-purple flowers, three yellow stamens and three orange-red stigmas…
body: To preserve the colour and flavour, the stigma must be dried immediately without damage. In hotter, drier countries, this was – and still is – done outside in the shade. An alternative method is to use mesh trays over charcoal, while in England kilns were used, and the resulting threads or “chives” were sold either as hay saffron or pressed between weighted boards. In a year-long project by the University of Cambridge, researchers found documents from as late as 1871 recording thefts of saffron from warehouses and druggists. But, just a few decades later, while a few individuals continued to grow saffron for their own use, commercial cultivation in Britain had ceased.

These days, growers such as David Smale, a geophysicist by training, are cultivating English saffron commercially, and it is Smale’s advice I followed this week when I made Richard Olney ’s recipe for buttered saffron rice and slivers of ripe, carefully peeled tomatoes: a delicate, delicious dish that can be served with poached chicken, fish or hard-boiled eggs.

articles.title: I tried 11 coffees from Counter Culture, the accessible small-batch roaster converting coffee slobs to snobs
articles.summary: I’ll never go back to Starbucks after trying this specialty brand. Level up your morning coffee with well-made beans and the right roast for you. Four ways to brew better drip coffee. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I’m an empathetic girl, except when it comes to anyone who despises the taste of coffee.

Having perfected my at-home cup, I can’t fathom anyone disliking the warming flavors that incentivize me to leave my bed every morning. In fact, I’m convinced I could convert tea loyalists and energy drink lovers into coffee connoisseurs if they set aside their Folgers and tried quality beans.

My journey to finding my favorite coffee started with the Starbucks Veranda blend I drank growing up. Then, one day, while browsing my local Whole Foods, I discovered Counter Culture Coffee, an independent specialty coffee brand. I was immediately hooked on its smooth, fresh blends that tasted like the iced coffees I would usually order from my favorite pricey cafes.

Quality aside, I appreciated that Counter Culture was a convenient, reliable option. Often on sale for $12-$16, I found it an accessible way to join the ranks of coffee snobs. While many coffee experts recommend purchasing from a local roaster, I often opt for the convenience of grabbing beans at the grocery store or online. They also offer two subscription options, delivering two bags to your doorstep for under $40 a month.

articles.title: My mum has died – and there is one kind of response I can’t stand | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: The platitudes, euphemisms and cliches are excruciating. But the people who say nothing at all are the worst. Luckily, I already knew having a comic thought at a tragic moment is a natural stress response, or I might have worried.
body: In Curb Your Enthusiasm, when Marty Funkhouser’s mother’s wheelchair was run over by a car, he proclaimed himself an orphan. David informed him he was too old to be an orphan. Funkhouser insisted that if your parents are dead, you’re an orphan.

Images of Annie-like red curls aside, the people who brought you into the world both having left it is pretty profound. I’m lucky to have a lot of support, but it’s a hard knock in life. A singularly specific brand of aloneness; the natural order that feels anything but. It’s so weird. There’s no one to tell me off any more, either. I wonder what I may get up to. What if I fall in with a bad crowd?

My mum “had a good innings though”, as I have been reminded roughly thrice daily. It’s been 14 years since my dad died, and there’s so much I’d forgotten about the grief game – namely the platitudes, the strange language, and how terrible so many of us are at dealing with it. The best reaction so far was a bloke who replied to my breaking of the news for sadmin purposes with: “OK, that’s fine.” At least he gave me a good story.
points: But the people who say nothing at all are the worst.
Luckily, I already knew having a comic thought at a tragic moment is a natural stress response, or I might have worried.

articles.title: 5 Emerging Designers on Running a Label in Japan
articles.summary: While Japan’s fashion scene is enjoying a global moment, harnessing international appeal has its fair share of obstacles. Five designers weigh in on what it takes to succeed.
body: Japan’s fashion industry is enjoying a global moment. An influx of tourism into the country buoyed by the weak yen has coincided with a booming cultural interest in Japanese fashion. The country has produced three winners of the LVMH Prize in the past decade, and with the success of recent menswear exports like Auralee and Ssstein breaking through on the Paris schedule, more names are on the way.

But for the country’s emerging designers, harnessing that international interest has its fair share of obstacles. What does it take to build a global fashion business from Japan today? Five designers weigh in below.

Background: Growing up between the US and China, Viviano Sue first moved to Tokyo to study at Bunka Fashion College. His eponymous brand trades in statement dresses and tailoring with unapologetic flounce, and in 2024 launched a menswear line. Worn by the likes of Lady Gaga, Bad Bunny, and Hudson Williams, Viviano’s recent strategy has targeted Hollywood.

articles.title: Artist Yayoi Kusama Has Died at 97
articles.summary: The renowned Japanese avant-gardist died on Wednesday at a hospital in Tokyo from multiple organ failure, according to her US gallery, David Zwirner. She was 97.
body: Renowned Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama died on Wednesday at a hospital in Tokyo, according to her gallery, David Zwirner. She was 97. Kusama’s work, with its fizzy pop-culture style and preponderance of polka dots, spanned painting, drawing, sculpture, and performance, as well as literature, fashion, and product design. Her artworks regularly fetched record-breaking prices at auction.

Born in Matsumoto City, Japan, in 1929, Kusama studied Nihonga, a formal style of Japanese painting, in Kyoto. She began painting at the age of 10, with her early works reflecting hallucinogenic visions that often took the form of dots. The motif—which she later described as representing the cosmos—would become her signature. “After all, well, the moon is a polka dot, the sun is a polka dot, and then, the Earth where we live is also a polka dot,” she told a journalist.

Kusama moved to New York in 1957, attracted by the city’s experimental art scene. Over the next decade, she became part of the New York avant-garde, first attracting notice with her Infinity Nets, a series of artworks featuring undulating, apparently endless patterns.
points: The renowned Japanese avant-gardist died on Wednesday at a hospital in Tokyo from multiple organ failure, according to her US gallery, David Zwirner.

articles.title: Why Guerlain Is Launching a New L’Heure Bleue
articles.summary: Coinciding with the house’s first women’s perfume launch in a decade, CEO Gabrielle Saint-Genis shares her strategy with Vogue Business.
body: L’Heure Bleue marks Guerlain’s first major women’s fragrance launch in nearly a decade, following that of Mon Guerlain in 2017. “We take our time at Guerlain, waiting until we have something truly meaningful to offer the world,” CEO Gabrielle Saint-Genis says. “When you’re a house that has been passionate about fragrance for 200 years, you are obsessed with innovating. And in this particular case, we wanted to pay tribute to this extraordinary creation by Jacques Guerlain.”

L’Heure Bleue is a new iteration of a cornerstone in Guerlain’s heritage: a fragrance created by Jacques Guerlain in 1912 that is still available today and is one of the house’s oldest, albeit lesser known, fragrances. “He created L’Heure Bleue after an immense emotional experience one evening while crossing the Pont Neuf, right there,” Saint-Genis says, speaking from her office, just a stone’s throw from the bridge, with a sweeping view of Paris.

articles.title: The 11 Best Skin-Care Ingredients That Support Collagen
articles.summary: Supporting collagen production is vital to skin health. Here, experts break down the best skin-care ingredients you need for firm, hydrated, and plump skin.
body: The right skin-care ingredients can help with collagen loss. Our collagen production may naturally start to decrease in our mid-to-late 20s, explains Morgan Rabach, MD, board-certified dermatologist at Rabach Aesthetics. When you add in air pollution, sun exposure, inflammation, stress, poor sleep, and other external factors, that’s when collagen really weakens and you’ll start to notice those first signs of aging: fine lines, sagging skin, etc. If you’re not facing severe skin laxity that requires the more intense skin-firming treatments, topical products will be your first line of defense.

“Using ingredients that support collagen improves skin quality over time,” Dr. Rabach says. “Supporting collagen will help improve hydration retention, skin texture, and firmness and reduce the appearance of wrinkles.”

articles.title: For Starry Waters and Tiny Glowing Squids, Head to These Best Places to See Bioluminescence
articles.summary: From the dazzling atolls of the Maldives to Mexican shores via the British Isles, these are the places to add to the bucket list for waters akin to starry skies.
body: It is generally safe to touch and swim in bioluminescent waters, especially in destinations where the sparkling waters are featured as tourist attractions with boat trips and excursions. However, some bioluminescence results from harmful algal blooms that can cause skin rashes and severe illness if ingested. When in doubt, research the area you’re visiting thoroughly and speak to guides on organized trips.

The picture-perfect islands of the Maldives are some of the best places to see bioluminescence around the world, thanks to an abundance of plankton that illuminates the waves after sunset. While it’s possible to see the phenomenon on islands across the archipelago, one of the most famous spots of them all is on the quietest side of Vaadhoo Island, a minuscule island of the Raa Atoll known for its beachy corner nicknamed the sea of stars.
